commits.message:
Markdown reads a link's destination and title as markdown-it does, as Rich does (rich-unfiled-791c.jlqz) (#434)

* Markdown reads a link's destination and title as markdown-it does, as Rich does (rich-unfiled-791c.jlqz)

linkDestination scanned a bare destination to the end of the text for every
`](` whose brackets matched, with no nesting cap, so `[*a](` repeated 20000
times took 14 s. destinationAt is now markdown-it's parseLinkDestination: at
most 32 parentheses open and all of them closed, ended only by an ASCII space
or control character or a backslash-space, and an angled destination that
honours escapes and is no destination without its `>`. LINK_TAIL is the link
rule's tail: a title only after a space, backslash escapes in it, markdown-it's
space rather than Unicode's. Every case is pinned to Rich 15's output.

* Markdown reads a link's tail in linear time and a lone CR as a line ending, as markdown-it does (rich-unfiled-791c.jlqz)

Review (high) fixes: the space after a destination is skipped once, as
markdown-it's link rule does, instead of split two ways by one regex — 100k
spaces took six seconds; one LINK_SPACE pattern is now the only definition
of link space; parseMarkdown ends a line at \r as markdown-it normalizes it.
